name: Introduction
problem:
Recall that the principal components of a standardized observation matrix $X$ are the unit eigenvectors of the covariance matrix $C.$ If 

$$
\lambda_1 \gt \lambda_2 \gt \cdots\gt \lambda_n
$$

are the eigenvalues of $C$ written in descending order, then: 

- the $1$st principal component is the unit eigenvector $\mathbf u_1$ corresponding to the $1$st eigenvalue $\lambda_1,$

- the $2$nd principal component is the unit eigenvector $\mathbf u_2$ corresponding to the $2$nd eigenvalue $\lambda_2,$

- $\cdots$

and so on.

For example, suppose that the covariance matrix $C$ of some particular observations is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14199091/assets/86cd114656be47342171ec85d1a597e98403f7b4bcd40e8eca9a48cf5c484c21.svg)

It's easy to show that the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix $C,$ in descending order, are 

$$
\lambda_1=10, \qquad
\lambda_2=8.
$$

To find the first principal component of the data, we need the unit eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda_1=10.$ 

Applying our usual algorithm for finding eigenvectors, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C-10I & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 1 \\ 1 & 9\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, seeking a non-zero solution of $(C-10I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14199091/assets/9609698d9ffecd2d7afceaa6c3bc343a737819f9b5bf6a1e77cc31c887233ad5.svg) 

Finally, dividing $\mathbf{v}_1$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_1 \| = \sqrt{2},$ we get 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14199091/assets/4eb734f1c0bc45ec8298850310816343c9b8d5da765c1b38dea8b18f192d299d.svg) 

Therefore, the $1$st principal component of the data is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14199091/assets/4f503d9e84c83f8b4409df389ae8f814dbbb91f27385534b0b0d8b06d004926b.svg)

**Note:** The opposite vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14199091/assets/1674dcbe0ef0bffa803460fc8939c915aa22aba9f8195cb5842f177d63b76f0c.svg) also works in the example above.
